messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I’d like to buy the house with my husband; it matters to us to make a home there, and a family discount would make that more workable. C’s agreement matters because I know she hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without it. I know B wants money, but not why, and I’d want to understand her needs too. I’m not sure about a summary yet. I don’t have a particular discomfort with being asked this way.

1) I want clarity and a fair share in Dad’s house and will. “Care and clarity…” fits.  
2) I won’t subsidize A and her husband’s discounted purchase. Fair, transparent treatment fits.  
3) I haven’t agreed to the discount, and won’t sign off on an arrangement that isn’t fair to me. Being heard and having a genuine choice fits.  
4) I can’t speak for B or assume what she needs. I want each sister treated fairly financially; that wording fits.  
5) I’d like this settled, but there’s no rush. “Move carefully” fits.  

No objection to asking A first, but don’t treat any guess as agreed until I confirm it.
